steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: ...I believe you're wrong, sir.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: Victoria may be the strongest nation on Terra, for now, but there is no guarantee that such prosperity will last forever.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: We are all familiar enough with the history of Victoria's four golden decades, nourished by the legacy of Gaul.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: Times have changed, however. When Victoria's productivity advantages eroded, and her ambition to expand went unsated, the cracks of internal strife began to emerge beneath the surface.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: The last king attempted to mediate between the factories and the merchants, but failed to propose a new path out of the dilemma.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: His end was inevitable. The same was demonstrated by the coup in Leithanien not long after.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: Who emerged as the victor of the bloody struggle? No... it has been more than a decade since they hanged the Lord of Lions, but the repercussions of the coup linger to this day.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: The Wheat of Brighton... the River Mersey Incident... have the dukes been able to set aside their conflicts for even a moment this past decade?

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: Everyone believes they will emerge the better for the struggle. Not one believes they're digging Victoria's grave together.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: If we do not see change soon, an intensifying civil war will be what defines Victoria in this new era.

steps.name: Powerful Old Woman
steps.text: I heard that a most eloquent young man stole the show today.

steps.name: Powerful Old Woman
steps.text: One would be forgiven for mistaking you for today's headliner.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: I meant no offence, Your Grace, Duke of Caster.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: I had hoped to make the acquaintance of more people of wisdom at your manor, but I confess I find myself disappointed.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Do you consider yourself worthy of a position as a duke's advisor, or even the Speaker of Parliament, then?

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: Anyone can point out the ills that plague this nation. Curing it, however, calls for the proper means... a stroke of luck, even.

steps.name: Elegant Young Man
steps.text: It seems that I am hardly the one who should be worrying about these things, though. What do you think?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Heh...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I remember your mother... you have inherited none of her humility or courtesy, but all of her boldness and irreverence.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...Enciodes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You would hardly have found time for a distant relative from a distant land, if I had not caught your attention this way.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: It was a rather inflammatory speech, but far from being enough to lay a foundation.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Many young lads have visited this house intending to make their names amongst the guests, so as to enjoy the adoration of others in high society.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: How do I know you are not one of them?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I have little interest in becoming a guest of honor at the banquets of Victorian nobility. I simply bring a modest proposal.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The resources of Kjerag and the industry of Caster complement each other perfectly. There is potential for equal cooperation.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I am building Kjerag's first transnational trading company, and I would like to extend an invitation.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...Equal?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Equal.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: In thirty years, the name Kjerag will lie on the lips of all the nations of Terra.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: We have nothing to lose, and everything to gain, from cooperation between our two lands.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I commend your courage.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: But I doubt you have the means to make such a promise, child.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You will assent.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: As a consummate and visionary politician, you are well aware of the dilemma that Victoria faces... or should I say, the duchy of Caster faces.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You would not lightly dismiss any measure that could improve the situation, however slim the chance.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The fact that I stand before you now is proof enough that I'm worth investing in.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Be thankful you are young enough that I can forgive your impudence.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Answer me, then, young visionary, with your wit and guile.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: How does a country that has yet to adopt the Originium circuit plan on becoming a name on the lips of all the nations of Terra?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Your doubts are well-founded. Industry and technology are certainly important, but for a nation, there are other things that are even more important.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: To be frank, the particular nature of Victorian politics may have clouded your eyes to the potential of a united nation.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I believe—

a.text: And She stood upon the highest peak, pointed to the lake in the distance, and spoke:
'Remember the path you walked, and let not yourself forget;
Fear the blizzard that has yet to come, and let not yourself be arrogant;
Clutch your bows and arrows, pickaxes and hoes tight, and let not yourself be careless;
Love your brothers and sisters; love your neighbors and friends, and love the rocks and hills, the grass and trees, as you would love your own siblings.
Heed these words, and no calamity shall befall you, and your home and hearth will be safe forever more.'

steps.name: Vine-Bead Court Elder
steps.text: Saintess, it's almost time...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Have the doctors not found a way?

steps.name: Vine-Bead Court Elder
steps.text: For years, the finest doctors of Kjerag and Victoria tried everything they could think of to purge the poison from the Great Elder.

steps.name: Vine-Bead Court Elder
steps.text: In the end, it is not illness that takes him, but time.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: May I see him?

steps.name: Vine-Bead Court Elder
steps.text: Of course...

steps.name: Vine-Bead Court Elder
steps.text: Please... deliver him in Kjeragandr's name.
Enya gently pushes the door open.
The dying man's chest barely moves as he lies on the bed. He seems to hear the sound and cocks his ear with great effort before opening his mouth meekly.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Enya... is that you?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Great Elder...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: How are you feeling? Would you like some water?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Listen to me, Enya...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: What is your wish?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: This day... has been too long in coming...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Do you think that? This day has been too long in coming...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Of course not...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You taught me many things.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: You have done well...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: But I was a poor teacher... a poor elder...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I was not even... a pious child of Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Great Elder?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I haven't heard Kjeragandr's voice... for many years...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I prayed day and night... recited the scriptures over and over... but She never answered my call.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I was lost... I was afraid...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: But I had to keep going...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I thought... if Kjeragandr's will was to protect Her people... it was not against Her will to act in such a way...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I wanted to strengthen the Vine-Bead Court's authority... I wanted the hearts of Kjerag to be united and firm...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: But I erred... in many ways...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: 'One can lie to a man, but no one can deceive Kjeragandr.'

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: She sees all that we do.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: She knows all our errors, and our repentance.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I know... I believed...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: But a long time passed... and I thought that I had not been punished by Kjeragandr...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: And so... I stopped believing.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Until last night... Kjeragandr came to me in a dream.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: She did not reproach me... She simply walked in front of me, leading me to the lake whose surface was like a mirror...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: And She said, 'All the rivers shall converge upon this place...'

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: And then I knew, my time was up...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I want to repent... I must repent... but it's too late for me...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Enya...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Tell me... honestly...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Do you still... hear Kjeragandr's voice?

a.text: Her followers must listen carefully to Her teachings at all times.
The noise of the land may deafen our ears to Her voice, and the wind and snow blind our eyes to Her teachings.
But remember always that She is good, and those who forsake Her walk on the wrong path.
It is harder to be good than evil, to forgive than to hate, to be humble than to be proud.
Those who tread this path must know it is a treacherous one, but those who stray from it shall find it even harder to return.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Stop making all that noise, Yucatan.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Since when are you as restless as Sciurus?

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: I'm sorry, Matriarch... but I just can't help myself at a time like this...

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: There's nothing I can do for her but pray.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Always so uneasy, you and Sciurus.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: She is my younger sister, and the future Browntail Matriarch. A little thing like this should be no trouble at all.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: That idiot's in excellent health. You remember how she sneaked out to climb Mount Jungfrau when she was eight, and ended up breaking her leg when she fell?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: They thought she'd never walk again. In two months, she was running and jumping around like nothing ever happened.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: No one gave it a second thought... are we really sure there were no lingering effects?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: No, no, of course there wouldn't be...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: It was so long ago, and the doctors say she's healthy as a burdenbeast...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: But can those Victorian doctors really be trusted? I'll have their heads if anything happens to my stupid sister...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Gopferdammi... it's been four hours! Why haven't they come out yet?

spans.text: it's been four hours! Why haven't they come out yet?

steps.name: Browntail Guard
steps.text: Matriarch, report from Captain Monch—

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Shut up! Don't bother me, whatever it is!

steps.name: Browntail Guard
steps.text: Understood...

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: L-Let's take a deep breath, Matriarch...

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Kjeragandr will protect Rus...

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: She's the gentlest woman I've ever met... who would Kjeragandr watch over, if not her?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You're right... you're right...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Kjeragandr...
O Kjeragandr... hear my prayer...
I am hardly the most pious of Kjeragandr's people, but now I muster all my piety, in the hopes that Kjeragandr will grant this one favor.
If Clan Browntail must be punished for our past transgressions, then let all that punishment fall upon me.
I will accept your anger, your wrath.
But please... spare my foolish sister...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: By Kjeragandr...
Dear travelers, please note that train KT392 departing from Lake Silberneherze bound for Brig Pass will be delayed by one hour due to inclement weather.
Kjerag Rail sincerely apologizes for the inconvenience.
Please speak to a staff member at the information desk if you require assistance...

steps.name: Impatient Tourist
steps.text: Are Victorian trains ever NOT late? Looks like they've rubbed off on Kjerag Rail.

steps.name: Leisurely Tourist
steps.text: It's just a little wait. Frankly, I'd rather stay here for a while longer than deal with those investors back home.

steps.name: Leisurely Tourist
steps.text: At least they have good cystymilk here for free... *burp*.

steps.name: Leisurely Tourist
steps.text: But inclement weather, they say? Doesn't look like it's snowing...

steps.name: Impatient Tourist
steps.text: What's the hurry? The trains aren't running.

steps.name: Agitated Woman
steps.text: Sorry... excuse me...

steps.name: Impatient Tourist
steps.text: Wait a minute...

steps.name: Impatient Tourist
steps.text: I've seen this trick before! You're a pickpocket, aren't you?

steps.name: Impatient Tourist
steps.text: Stop right there! Let me make sure you didn't steal anything...
The woman breaks free of the hand grabbing her shoulder and runs in the direction of the crowd, vanishing into a sea of people.

steps.name: Impatient Tourist
steps.text: Huh! Hey! Somebody, help! Thief!

steps.name: Staff
steps.text: Did you lose something, ma'am?

steps.name: Impatient Tourist
steps.text: My purse, jewelry, terminal... huh? Everything seems to be here?

steps.name: Impatient Tourist
steps.text: But that one...

steps.name: Leisurely Tourist
steps.text: Probably some unfortunate sod trying to get on without a ticket.

steps.name: Leisurely Tourist
steps.text: I told you, this is pious Kjerag, not postwar Londinium. No one's after your purse.

steps.name: Leisurely Tourist
steps.text: By Kjeragandr...

steps.name: Leisurely Tourist
steps.text: Does trying to ride without a ticket get you hunted down by warriors, in Kjerag?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Found you.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Madam Carolin of Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I know who you are, and what you've done. Come quietly, unless you want everyone under the sun to know.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: The Vine-Bead Court will grant you a fair and impartial trial. First, give me what you're holding.
The woman silently clutches the folder in her arms and thinks for a moment before crying out without warning.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Run!

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Run! There's a bomb in the station!
The crowded station quickly descends into chaos at the woman's cry.
The creator of the chaos once again disappears into the crowd.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Damn...

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Rus... so glad you're alright...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: How are they... the children?

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Perfectly fine. Your sister's taking care of them.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Rest now, and don't worry about a thing.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Yucatan... there were a few times there I thought I was going to see Kjeragandr...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Every little bad thing that I ever did came flashing back before my eyes... even that time when I climbed that tree to steal fowlbeast eggs when I was eight...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: What would Kjeragandr punish me for...?

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: She already punished you, remember? That time you spent two months in bed.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Don't worry about it, Rus... we've made it through so much. Now we've got another reason to keep going.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: We have to see Oak and Berry grow up.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Kjeragandr won't separate us...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Yucatan... is it snowing outside?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: It's a little cold...

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: I'll add some firewood and get you another blanket.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Sleep well, Rus.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: The winter will pass... and we can go see the flowers by the lake when spring comes. All of us, together.
Sciurus closes her eyes and falls asleep quietly.
It should be a moment of happiness...
But Yucatan feels a rock in his heart.
He looks outside. The clouds are thick and heavy, but the snow refuses to fall. This kind of weather is rarely seen in Kjerag.
Maybe we're in for a cold winter this year, Yucatan thinks.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: When the winter passes...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: 'She is omnipresent, She cannot be sought.'

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: We need not question Her existence. She is there when we choose to follow Her.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...Do you remember this from the scriptures?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: No... this is not how it should be...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: If She is omnipresent and cannot be sought, then who hears Her will, and who—*cough* *cough*!!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You should rest, Great Elder. Don't let yourself suffer.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I see it, Enya...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I see unprecedented calamity descending upon Mount Karlan...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I see Originium bringing ruin to the land...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I see... I see Her abandoning Kjerag!
Caught up in a bout of excitement, the old man stares outside the window, his face warped and twisted, seemingly seething in anger, or engulfed by a terror that defies description.
He raises his withered arms, trying to grasp something, only for them to fall back down meekly.
Finally, he quiets down, as though he has expended the last sliver of strength he had...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Great Elder...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Enya...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Say a prayer for me...

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: The final chapter... of the Kjeragandr...

a.text: '...And all the rivers shall converge upon this place at the end of it all;
And you shall walk the path forward alone,
And the path you shall walk lies beneath your feet.'
She sighs as She speaks the words.
She turns around, and disappears in the wind and snow from whence she came.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: You have no hope of escape. The people of Kjerag know the wind and snow better than any outsider. Your Arts are not effective here.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: We don't want to damage our relationship with Rhine Lab. Otherwise, I would keep you here by any means necessary to retrieve the military secrets that you stole.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: ...I'm not carrying your military secrets.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I have no reason to believe you.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: You don't understand.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Don't understand what?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: You don't understand what these data mean...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: How long do you think your 'god' will protect you?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: You can't talk your way out of this—

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Wait...

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: What's with the clouds...?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Run—
The avalanche struck in an instant.
A loud crack moved the mountains that had remained dormant for many years. Snow poured down the slopes, mixed with rocks and black crystals, and all creation was obscured by gray and white.
The mountains trembled, the echoes lingered in the valley.
Few could comprehend what had just happened—
It was the first Catastrophe in history to strike this place.
